subject: Single aesthetic defined by multiple categorical variables

messages.author: 5a1f218c896ccb1a
messages.subject: Single aesthetic defined by multiple categorical variables
parts:
I have an MRI dataset, with id variables 'id', 'protocol',
'parameter', 'tissue', 'day', 'run' and measured value 'peak'.

I want to plot point or jitter plots, faceted by parameter and tissue,
with x = id, y = peak, colour = protocol and shape defined by both day
and run, i.e. day 1 run 1 = square, day 1 run 2 = triangular, day 2
run 1 = circular etc.

How can one define the aesthetic parameter shape by two categorical
variables?

qplot(id, peak, data=mri, colour=protocol, shape=???,
geom=c("jitter"), size=0.3, xlab="Patient ID", ylab="Peak Height",
facets =tissue~parameter)

Many thanks!

On Mon, Jul 11, 2011 at 9:39 AM, FRGS <fergus....@gmail.com> wrote:
> I have an MRI dataset, with id variables 'id', 'protocol',
> 'parameter', 'tissue', 'day', 'run' and measured value 'peak'.
>
> I want to plot point or jitter plots, faceted by parameter and tissue,
> with x = id, y = peak, colour = protocol and shape defined by both day
> and run, i.e. day 1 run 1 = square, day 1 run 2 = triangular, day 2
> run 1 = circular etc.
>
> How can one define the aesthetic parameter shape by two categorical
> variables?

Create a new factor that combines the levels of the two categorical
variables of interest and then use that new factor for the shape
aesthetic. See ?interaction.

HTH,
Dennis
